note: Montana licenses these programs under their own category - Private Alternative Adolescent Residential or Outdoor Programs - so there is a regulator whose job is specifically this industry. Oversight moved in 2019: the legislature dissolved the old PAARP board at the Department of Labor and gave licensing to DPHHS, which has since revoked a program's licence outright. Complaints to the Licensure Bureau are always anonymous, and the corrective actions it imposes are published.

civil_injury.summary: Two years from the injury for assault, battery or false imprisonment. Negligence and other personal injury claims have three years.
civil_injury.quote: (1) Except as provided in 27-2-216, the period prescribed for the commencement of an action upon a liability not founded upon an instrument in writing is within 3 years. ... (3) The period prescribed for the commencement of an action for libel, slander, assault, battery, false imprisonment, or seduction is within 2 years.
civil_injury.note: Montana Code Annotated 2025. A version effective October 1, 2026 (Ch. 709, L. 2025) adds an exception for § 27-2-219 (gender transition treatment claims) but does not change the 2- and 3-year periods. Montana's accrual/discovery rule (§ 27-2-102) was not read.

civil_minor_tolling.summary: The time while the injured person is a minor does not count, so the clock starts at 18: assault or battery claims by the 20th birthday, negligence claims by the 21st. There is no longer deadline for non-sexual physical abuse of a child.
civil_minor_tolling.quote: If a person entitled to bring an action mentioned in part 2, except 27-2-211(3), is, at the time the cause of action accrues, either a minor or has been committed pursuant to 53-21-127, the time of the disability is not a part of the time limit for commencing the action.
civil_minor_tolling.note: No cap on minority tolling (the 5-year cap applies only to commitment). § 27-2-216 (to age 27 or 3 years from discovery) covers childhood sexual abuse only.

civil_government_claims.summary: A claim against the State must first be presented in writing to the Department of Administration, which has 120 days to decide (the deadline to sue pauses for those 120 days); claims against a county or city are filed with its clerk. The ordinary 2- or 3-year periods still apply.
civil_government_claims.quote: A complaint based on a claim subject to the provisions of subsection (1) may not be filed in district court unless the claimant has first presented the claim to the department of administration and the department has finally denied the claim. ... Upon the department's receipt of the claim, the statute of limitations on the claim is tolled for 120 days.
civil_government_claims.note: No separate short notice deadline was found in § 2-9-301; the claim must simply be presented before suing and within the normal limitations period.

criminal_child_abuse.summary: Five years from the crime for felony assault on a minor (victim under 14, offender an adult) or other felony child abuse. Misdemeanor child endangerment: one year. The clock does not wait until the child turns 18.
criminal_child_abuse.citation: Mont. Code Ann. § 45-1-205(2); Mont. Code Ann. § 45-5-212
criminal_child_abuse.quote: (2) Except as provided in subsection (7)(b) or as otherwise provided by law, prosecutions for other offenses are subject to the following periods of limitation: (a) A prosecution for a felony must be commenced within 5 years after it is committed. (b) A prosecution for a misdemeanor must be commenced within 1 year after it is committed.
criminal_child_abuse.note: Assault on a minor (§ 45-5-212) is punished by imprisonment 'in a state prison for a term not to exceed 5 years' (up to 40 years for very young victims), so it is a felony. Endangering the welfare of children (§ 45-5-622) covers a 'parent, guardian, or other person supervising the welfare of a child'; the basic offense is a misdemeanor ('imprisoned in the county jail for any term not to exceed 6 months', § 45-5-622(6)(a)), so one year; the felony tier in § 45-5-622(6)(b) applies to subsection (3), which covers specific conduct (drug-related exposure, among others) not read in full. The no-limit rule for victims under 18 (§ 45-1-205(1)(c)) covers sex offenses only. The period does not run while the offender lives outside Montana (§ 45-1-206(1)).

criminal_felony_assault.summary: Five years from the crime for aggravated assault or any other felony. Misdemeanor assault: one year.
criminal_felony_assault.quote: (a) A prosecution for a felony must be commenced within 5 years after it is committed. (b) A prosecution for a misdemeanor must be commenced within 1 year after it is committed.
criminal_felony_assault.note: Excluded periods: offender not resident in Montana, or a pending prosecution for the same conduct (§ 45-1-206).

channels.name: Montana Board of Behavioral Health (Department of Labor and Industry)
channels.what_it_can_do: The Department and its licensing boards take action against unprofessional, incompetent or unlawful practice, up to discipline of the licence. The Board of Behavioral Health covers mental health counselors, licensed professional counselors, addiction counselors and social workers; psychologists have their own board, and the same complaint route serves both.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: To bring formal charges the Department needs evidence in the form of a document or a statement - a complaint with nothing behind it will not get far.
channels.who_to_report: Anyone holding a Montana behavioral health or psychology licence. The Department's licence search shows current status and any disciplinary history.
channels.how: Use the online licence complaint form. There is a downloadable paper form as an alternative, and an FAQ written for complainants rather than licensees.
channels.mail: Board of Behavioral Health, 301 S. Park Avenue, 4th Floor, Helena, MT 59620
channels.note: This board covers the clinician, not the program. A complaint about a facility goes to the DPHHS Licensure Bureau instead, and the Department's own page says so.

channels.name: Montana DPHHS, Quality Assurance Division, Licensure Bureau
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and regulates private alternative adolescent residential and outdoor programs, inspects them, imposes corrective action and can revoke a licence. It has done so: Montana permanently revoked one program's licence and removed the children from another.
channels.who_to_report: The program itself - conditions, staffing, supervision, how it treats the young people in it.
channels.how: Contact the Licensure Bureau by phone or post. The corrective actions it imposes are published on the Bureau's website, so it is worth reading what a program has already been cited for.
channels.mail: DPHHS Licensure Bureau, PO Box 202953, Helena, MT 59620-2953
channels.note: DPHHS states that complaints against the programs it licenses are always kept anonymous.

channels.name: Montana Child Abuse and Neglect Hotline (Centralized Intake)
channels.what_it_can_do: The statutory intake line for child abuse and neglect. Where a complaint covers both abuse and a licensing breach, the Child and Family Services Division leads the child protection side of the investigation and the Licensure Bureau handles the licence.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a Montana program right now. Montana's own rules require the programs themselves to report suspected abuse to this number.
channels.how: Call. It takes reports around the clock.

channels.name: Montana Office of the Child and Family Ombudsman
channels.what_it_can_do: An independent office in the Department of Justice that reviews how the child protection system handles a case and publishes its findings. Useful when a report has already been made and nothing happened.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It reviews the state's handling rather than investigating the program directly, and it does not licence anybody.
channels.who_to_report: A family or young person who reported something and has hit a wall.
channels.how: File a request for assistance online.

channels.name: Disability Rights Montana
channels.what_it_can_do: Montana's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A Montana program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
